longName: Recognize Completed Workplace Training as a Verifiable Credential in the Employee's Wallet
scope: One employer's LMS issuing one training-completion LER to one employee's wallet. PROPOSED — the issue states no scope.

keyConcepts.definition: The three-party structure of verifiable-credential exchange: an Issuer who asserts, a Holder who keeps and presents, and a Verifier who checks — supported by registries that supply identity, skill definitions, and trust signals.

openIssues: No trigger is stated in the source issue; the value below is PROPOSED from the Introduction narrative and needs author confirmation.

Six cited CEDS rows — the Credential Condition Profile / Option / Option-Component family — did not resolve against the DME standards graph and carry no definition or URL in the issue itself. They are carried as OrphanElements, which is exactly what the standard asks for: a data need is never silently dropped, it goes into an editorial queue. A question for the standards team — either a coverage gap in the DME's loaded CEDS, or newer or renamed terms.

Brandon (issue comment): this use case can connect with CTDL, OB3, CASE, SCD, and PESC. Only OB3 is cited so far; the other four are natural additions in a second pass, each adding a REQUIRES_STANDARD edge once confirmed.

The Introduction describes proficiency demonstrated 'in an online simulation exercise' — an assessment event that precedes and justifies issuance, which no step models. It may well be out of scope (the LMS's own assessment case), or the family may want an assessment predecessor. An open and rather interesting question.

actors.role: An employer's Learning Management System, issuing a training-completion LER into the employee's wallet.
actors.interest: Training the employer paid for produces portable, verifiable evidence.

actors.role: A retail employee receiving, reviewing, and storing the training credential.
actors.interest: I hold verifiable evidence of training I completed, to show this and future employers.

actors.role: Provides identity verification for the know-your-customer step.
actors.interest: Identity assertions it supplies are relied upon correctly.

actors.role: Provides the customer-service skill definitions and their proficiency metadata.
actors.interest: Credentials cite registered skill definitions rather than free text.

actors.role: Publishes the Issuer's DID and public key as a trust signal.
actors.interest: Verifiers can later confirm the Issuer's signature.

interestedParties.interest: Can accept demonstrated customer-service proficiency without re-training the worker.
Training investment is recorded in a form the workforce can carry and the employer can audit.

triggeredBy.name: Employee completes a training unit and demonstrates proficiency in the LMS simulation exercise

assumes.statement: The employee has completed the employer-provided training unit and demonstrated proficiency in the online simulation exercise.

scenario.condition: the Holder does not recognize the claims as their own
